summary: Camels have special bodies for desert life, and they have been important to the people of Arabia for thousands of years.
introduce: Show the title “Camels: Built for the Desert” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: the power a body needs to move, work, and grow
to keep someone or something safe from harm
the buying, selling, or swapping of goods between people or places

challengeTerms.def: a body feature or behavior that helps a living thing survive where it lives
doing a job well without wasting time, energy, or materials
tamed and raised by people instead of living in the wild

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that camels are still important to life in Saudi Arabia today? Use evidence from the article to explain.
The camel is called "the ship of the desert." Explain why this nickname fits.
struggling: Pre-teach energy, protect, and trade with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses adaptation, efficient, and domesticated to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
